sites.name: Bankers Lode Claim
overview: Bankers Lode Claim is a historic underground mining property in Jefferson County's Ralston Buttes mining district, developed along a north-trending breccia zone in Precambrian crystalline rock.
timeline: The mine was developed with a drift about 500 feet long, two raises, and a crosscut; later published descriptions reported the workings as extensively collapsed.
In 1954, federal uranium-reconnaissance work included a preliminary report and geologic map of the Bankers Lode workings in the district.
moreHistory: Published geologic descriptions place the Bankers Lode Claim in the SE quarter of the NW quarter of section 9, Township 2 South, Range 71 West, at roughly 8,500 feet elevation. Reported mineralization includes fluorite and copper minerals such as chalcocite, with secondary malachite and cuprite among the noted minerals.

sites.name: Aubrey-Ladwig Mine
sites.location: Ralston Buttes Mining District near Golden
overview: The Aubrey-Ladwig Mine was a documented uranium producer in Jefferson County's Ralston Buttes Mining District, developed during the 1950s uranium boom.
U.S. Geological Survey records describe open-pit and underground workings, uranium-bearing fault and fracture mineralization, and production beginning after a 1954 discovery on the property.

timeline.text: USGS records state that uranium was discovered on the Aubrey Ladwig property in the fall of 1954.
After trenching and drilling, production began in the fall of 1955 under a lease held by the Denver-Golden Oil and Uranium Company.
Federal mineral records report uranium ore from this period and describe both surface and underground development at the property.
USGS and Colorado Geological Survey publications continued to document the Ladwig deposit as an important studied uranium occurrence in the Ralston Buttes district.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 520 and later USGS work describe the Aubrey-Ladwig deposit as uranium mineralization hosted by fractures and faults associated with Precambrian gneiss and pegmatite.

MRDS records derived from federal mineral inventories describe exploratory pits and trenches, a principal open pit, a vertical shaft with crosscut and drift development, and an inclined stope. Historic ore records for 1955-1956 reported uranium grades in the range documented by those federal records.

The mapped Aubrey Ladwig Mine point near 39.79110, -105.26555 is used as a defensible mine-level identification anchor. It should not be interpreted as a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar, portal, or statement of current access conditions.

sites.name: Beryl Ores Mill
sites.location: Arvada-area beryl and mica processing plant, Jefferson County
overview: Beryl Ores Mill was a Jefferson County mineral-processing plant operated by Beryl Ores, Inc. near Arvada, where beryl and mica ores were purchased and processed during the mid-twentieth century.

Colorado Bureau of Mines annual reports document the plant as part of Jefferson County's mineral industry in the late 1950s and early 1960s, while later federal records identify Beryl Ores Company as a Colorado location associated with beryllium handling.

timeline.text: The Colorado Bureau of Mines reported that Beryl Ores, Inc. processed beryl and mica ores at its plant near Arvada.
The state mining report noted that Beryl Ores, Inc. near Arvada purchased beryl and mica ore from operations in Jefferson and surrounding counties.
The Colorado Bureau of Mines again recorded the Beryl Ores Company in Arvada purchasing and processing beryl ore.
A federal beryllium emissions inventory listed Beryl Ores Company in Arvada among Colorado companies dealing in beryllium and beryllium alloys.

moreHistory: Federal mineral-record data preserve the plant as Beryl Ores Mill, also rendered as Beryllium Ores Mill, with Beryl Ores Company identified as owner-operator and beryllium as the primary commodity.

The federal mineral record places the plant across portions of Sections 17 and 18, Township 2 South, Range 69 West, and provides a site-level reference point near 39.8777, -105.1438. That point is used as the mapped location of the historic processing site and should not be interpreted as a surveyed surviving structure or a statement of present-day access.

Later federal occupational records continued to identify Beryl Ores Company in Colorado, showing that the company name remained associated with beryllium-related industrial activity after the period documented by the state mining reports.

sites.name: Big Bear No. 2 Mine
sites.location: South Platte Pegmatite District, Jefferson County
overview: Big Bear No. 2 is a rare-earth-element and feldspar pegmatite mine in Jefferson County's South Platte Pegmatite District. Published records also use the names Big Bear and Little Bear for the locality.

The deposit is documented as a complex pegmatite worked by two open cuts, with microcline and rare-earth-bearing minerals including xenotime, monazite, gadolinite, allanite and yttrium-bearing fluorite.

timeline.text: USGS Bulletin 1181-C documented the geology of the Platte Canyon quadrangle, one of the published sources later cited for the Big Bear No. 2 locality.
Colorado Geological Survey Resource Series 11 described the rare-earth pegmatites of the South Platte district, including Big Bear No. 2.

moreHistory: Mineral Resources Data System-derived records place Big Bear No. 2 near the head of an unnamed tributary of Spring Creek, about 1.9 miles north-northwest of Long Scraggy Peak, and identify the workings as two open cuts.

The larger pegmatite is described as having a quartz-microcline-biotite wall zone and microcline-quartz core cut by a replacement unit rich in fluorite, yttrium-bearing fluorite and other rare-earth minerals. A smaller pegmatite to the southeast is described as having a similar replacement unit and amethyst.

The coordinate shown here is the published mine-location point from the MRDS-derived record and is suitable for identifying the documented locality; it should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every historic excavation or mineralized exposure survives at that exact point today.

sites.name: Augusta Mine
sites.location: Evergreen Mining District near Cub Creek south of Evergreen
overview: The Augusta Mine, also known as the Augusta Lode Mine, is a historic fluorspar and base-metal mine in Jefferson County's Evergreen Mining District near Cub Creek south of Evergreen.
Federal and mineral-history sources document the mine as an early lead-zinc-copper prospect that later produced fluorspar from a steep fissure vein in Precambrian crystalline rock.

timeline.text: Published USGS history reports that the Augusta workings produced more than 1,000 tons of fluorspar during the early twentieth century after earlier development for lead, zinc, and copper.
Later locality records document limited additional production at the Augusta / Evergreen fluorite deposit in 1943.

moreHistory: USGS descriptions place the Augusta workings along a fissure vein south of Evergreen near Cub Creek. The vein strikes northwest and dips steeply southwest through Precambrian hornblende-biotite granite and gneiss.

Reported minerals and commodities include fluorite, copper and silver minerals, lead and zinc minerals, and minor gold. Historical descriptions note purple and green fluorspar veins and indicate that the old workings later became extensively collapsed.

The mapped identification point near 39.6175, -105.31722 is used as a defensible site-level reference supported by the USGS MRDS-derived Augusta record and independent mapped-place records. It should not be interpreted as a field-surveyed surviving portal, shaft collar, property boundary, or statement of current access.

sites.name: Big Bertha Mine
overview: Big Bertha Mine is a historic pegmatite mine in Jefferson County's South Platte district, where feldspar and rare-earth-bearing minerals were developed from a large pegmatite body in Pikes Peak Granite.
Colorado Geological Survey mapping documents the Big Bertha pegmatite in detail, including its open cut and internal quartz-microcline-biotite zones.

timeline.text: Federal mineral-record data derived from Colorado Division of Mines reports record 856 tons of feldspar production from Big Bertha in 1947 for glass manufacture.
Federal mineral records describe Big Bertha as a past producer, with feldspar production during this period and Consolidated Feldspar Corporation listed as operator beginning in 1953.
The Big Bertha pegmatite was geologically mapped in detail during Colorado Geological Survey research later published in Resource Series 11.
Colorado Geological Survey Resource Series 11 published a site-specific map and description of Big Bertha as a rare-earth pegmatite mined for rare-earth minerals.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey describes Big Bertha in the southwest quarter of the northwest quarter of Section 22, Township 8 South, Range 70 West, and characterizes the pegmatite as an irregular body with a small wall zone, very large allanite masses, and minor fluorite-xenotime replacement units.

CGS records identify Big Bertha as one of the South Platte pegmatites mined for rare-earth minerals and specifically note xenotime production. Federal mineral-record data also describe an open cut developed mainly in the quartz-microcline core.

The identification point at approximately 39.33944, -105.21778 is used as a defensible mine-level reference derived from the USGS MRDS record as reproduced by Western Mining History. It is not presented as a field-surveyed surviving portal, shaft collar, property boundary, or statement of current access.
